title: The Last Graft of the Brass Orchard
assumptions: Four adventurers; standalone fantasy, system-neutral automatic outcomes and concrete choices, no official combat rules or imported character sheets. Target a three-hour one-shot, with roughly 2,000 words of complete DM guide; session length must be established by human play, not asserted as fact.
prompt: Author a complete one-shot in an abandoned horticultural custody house. The party has agreed to retrieve the last living graft of an unusual orchard for a small community that wants to plant it. Someone else at the site has a legitimate competing interest in its future. Make the party's decisions matter beyond simply finding the object, without making a lecture or a mandatory fight the resolution. Use the supplied fixed five-room map unchanged: the Repository's Prepared Objective is the graft, the Side Annex offers an exploration interaction and the Inner Gate Key, and the Inner Hall supports an evidence-based puzzle. The puzzle must belong naturally to this place, with concrete evidence available to the players, not a disconnected riddle or a newly invented extra gate. Include the mapped secret bypass as an actual discoverable alternative. Choose the people, their knowledge, the recent situation and the practical stakes yourself within this preparation. Supply everything needed to run the choices and ending rather than asking the DM to finish the premise. Do not assume an existing campaign or import official rules or stat blocks.
guidance: Concise, concrete and inviting to read aloud. Distinguish arrival observations from private explanations and conditional revelations. Let players investigate, negotiate or take practical action rather than guessing the author's prescribed response. Use the existing geometry; portable objects and inhabitants may support play, but do not invent unrepresented terrain or machinery networks. Do not frame the finished guide as an evaluation exercise.
comparison_caveat: Fresh single-case strongest-model feasibility sample, consistency guidance on. Not an on/off comparison, not held-out reliability evidence, and not matched to the Last Pay Chest or historical Tier A packets. No scripted answer is supplied.
